provenance: Real output of EliteVault's Meta Campaign Scenario Modeler for one audited store (identity withheld). MODELED projection, not campaign results. Numbers come from the deterministic engine (lib/meta/simulation-engine.ts); the text around them is written by the AI.

conservative.summary: Under the conservative scenario with a spend of $420.00, we project a revenue of $253.20 resulting in 7.23 purchases at a CPA of $58.06. This yields a 0.6x ROAS (range 0.48x-0.72x), reflecting a net loss for week 1.
conservative.win_condition: Achieve a 1.0x ROAS by day 7 by rapidly killing underperforming creative variants and tightening targeting to core home decor buyers.
risks: Days 1-3 will see high CPA and volatility as the algorithm enters its mandatory learning phase.
iOS attribution under-reporting will mask true mobile conversion volume, making the net loss look worse on-platform.
Generic dropshipping store layout and fake countdown timers kill trust instantly among high-intent home buyers.
conservative.recommendation: Before increasing spend, fix the store's trust signals by removing fake countdown timers and upgrading product photography. Restrict budget to $420.00 until CPA drops below $40.

balanced.summary: The balanced scenario projects a spend of $700.00 generating $445.45 in revenue from 12.73 purchases with a CPA of $55.00. This results in a 0.64x ROAS (range 0.48x-0.8x), marking another clear week 1 loss.
balanced.win_condition: Maintain a stable CPA below $40 while scaling spend to $700.00, requiring at least one creative to drop below a $35 acquisition cost.
risks: Scaling spend too early in the week 1 learning phase will accelerate cash burn without improving conversion rates.
iOS privacy restrictions will continue to hide actual attributed revenue, skewing internal blended MER calculations.
Low-trust tactics on the site will repel high-income demographic traffic driven by broader Meta targeting.
balanced.recommendation: Keep daily budgets capped and focus entirely on testing lifestyle-oriented video hooks rather than gadget angles to improve the conversion rate.

aggressive.summary: The aggressive projection allocates $980.00 in spend, returning $634.96 in revenue across 18.14 purchases at a CPA of $54.02. This produces a 0.65x ROAS (range 0.42x-0.87x), confirming a heavy net loss.
aggressive.win_condition: Break even by hitting the upper range 0.87x ROAS, requiring immediate scaling of winning ad variations by day 4.
risks: Aggressive scaling on a site with a 56/100 audit score will rapidly amplify unprofitable traffic acquisition.
Severe signal loss from iOS attribution will obscure the true profitability of top-of-funnel cold campaigns.
Fatigue on initial cold ad sets will spike frequency and push CPAs far past the projected $54.02 threshold.
aggressive.recommendation: Do not run the aggressive budget tier until the store transitions from a dropshipping aggregator to an authentic lifestyle brand with verifiable social proof.
